texts: In Behcet disease the leading cause of death is the rupture of an arterial aneurysm: D.
Behcet disease, Morgan's hatchet, inflames vessels of every size; its aneurysms, in the aorta and in the pulmonary arteries, rupture readily: the burst bubble over the coffin.
Syphilitic aortitis is an inflammation that destroys the aortic media and leaves saccular aneurysms of the ascending aorta.
Takayasu arteritis mainly narrows and blocks the aorta and its branches; aneurysms are less common.
Mycotic aneurysms are usually saccular and focal, not diffuse and fusiform, and giant cell arteritis does raise the risk of a thoracic aortic aneurysm.
Memory hook: Morgan's hatchet pops the bubble: in Behcet disease, rupture kills.
